working_title: County Down's Golf Circuit: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: Most UK golfers who make the trip to County Down book Royal County Down and nothing else, then wonder why the trip felt so short. This post makes the case for treating the county as a proper three-course links circuit, with Royal County Down as the centrepiece but Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle as worthy rounds in their own right rather than mere fillers.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (RCD), Newcastle: opened 1889; Championship Links par 71, approximately 7,186 yards from championship tees; consistently ranked in the world's top 5 links courses; also has the shorter Annesley Links (par 66 equivalent, second course). Set against the Mountains of Mourne on Murlough Nature Reserve.
- RCD visitor days (Championship Links): Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday. Annesley Links: Monday, Thursday, Friday, Sunday. No visitor play Wednesday or Saturday.
- RCD 2026 green fees: Championship Links £450 per round; Annesley Links £120. Booking via enquiry form on club website; no ballot system; availability very limited so enquire early and offer multiple dates.
- RCD forecaddie fee: £110 per group (paid directly in cash to caddie after round). No on-site ATM; cash points in Newcastle town.
- RCD dress code: collared shirts required; no denim, collarless T-shirts, cargo shorts, tracksuits or leggings; soft-spiked shoes strongly advised; hats/caps removed indoors.
- RCD course character: blind tee shots on several holes (aiming posts used), deep 'bearded' bunkers with overhanging lips of marram/heather, fast domed greens, narrow fairways bordered by purple heather and golden gorse. Caddie strongly recommended for first visit.
- All play on both RCD courses in four-ball groups; groups of fewer than four may be combined.
- Nearby accommodation: Slieve Donard Resort and Spa (4-star, walking distance from first tee); Burrendale Hotel (3-star, approximately one mile from RCD gates).
- Ardglass Golf Club: clifftop 18-hole links on the north-east coast of County Down, founded 1896, par 70, 6,268 yards. Irish Sea in play on approximately eight holes. Around 30 minutes from RCD Newcastle, under an hour from Belfast.
- Ardglass clubhouse: occupies part of a fortified building, initial construction dated to 1405 — one of the oldest clubhouses in use anywhere.
- Ardglass green fees: prices have varied across sources; one 2025 visitor review mentions £160–£200 range; Golfshake lists midweek £115, weekend £140 as a guide — treat these as indicative only and verify directly with club before publishing.
- Ardglass character: sea views from every hole; Irish Sea comes into play; clifftop tees; hole 2 is a par 3 played over a gorge; frequently cited as a natural warm-up or wind-down round on an RCD itinerary.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club: 18 holes, par 70, 6,167 yards; located at Cloughey on the eastern shore of the Ards Peninsula. Founded 1902; redesigned by James Braid in 1934. Described as the most easterly 18-hole course in Ireland. Sandy base means playable year-round, virtually 365 days.
- Kirkistown visitor green fees: broadly in the £35–£50 range depending on day/season (multiple sources confirm sub-£50 for most visitor rounds); verify exact current fees with club directly.
- Kirkistown character: compact and quirky James Braid links; two nine-hole loops returning to clubhouse; several elevated greens (2nd, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th); rough particularly punishing; open to visitors seven days a week.
- Kirkistown is home club of Rory McIlroy's coach Michael Bannon; 2024 Curtis Cup player Beth Coulter is also associated with the club.
- Getting there: Newcastle (RCD) is approx. 30 miles south of Belfast. Ardglass is a further ~15 miles around the coast from Newcastle. Kirkistown is on the Ards Peninsula, roughly 25–30 miles north-east of Ardglass (allow 45 min by road). The circuit works best as a two- or three-night stay in the county.
- Getting to Northern Ireland from GB: ferry from Cairnryan or Liverpool to Belfast/Larne; or fly to Belfast International or George Best Belfast City Airport.
- No fixed public transport links between the three courses — a hire car is essential.
- Currency note for UK visitors: Northern Ireland uses pound sterling, same as mainland GB, so no currency exchange needed.
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate or present as confirmed any specific green fees beyond what can be cited as approximate/indicative ranges from research; instruct readers to verify directly with each club before booking. The £450 RCD Championship Links 2026 fee is well-sourced and may be stated; Ardglass and Kirkistown fees should be described as approximate ranges only.
- Do not invent quotes attributed to any real person (player, reviewer, or club staff).
- Do not claim personal testing or first-hand play of any of these courses.
- No gambling or betting content.
- No medical/injury advice beyond generic warm-up guidance.
- No financial advice on affordability; describe costs factually only.
- No affiliate links unless the relevant operator or booking platform is in the approved-partners list — mention any booking services informationally with no link if not pre-approved.
- Do not use em dashes anywhere in the post.
- UK English spelling throughout (favour, recognise, etc.).
- Northern Ireland is not the Republic of Ireland — do not conflate the two or suggest the courses are in 'Ireland' without specifying Northern Ireland.
- Avoid duplicating the angle of the existing Southwest Ireland post (Kerry/Clare) or any existing Wales/Scotland links circuit posts — this is specifically the County Down, Northern Ireland circuit.
